category: newsletter sender with a REST API

free_tier.stated: free for the first 100 subscribers, with the price assuming at most one email a day to the whole subscriber base; API included, no card
free_tier.notes: The quota counts subscribers, not messages. Sending from a custom domain is free; without one, mail goes out from the account's username at buttondown.email. Attachments, tagging and segmentation, automations and archives on a custom domain are paid add-ons. Subscribers are confirmed by double opt-in unless created through the API with type regular.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: email attachments are a paid add-on

interface_detail: the REST API at https://api.buttondown.com/v1 with an OpenAPI spec: POST /v1/emails creates an email for the subscriber base, and POST /v1/subscribers/{id_or_email}/emails/{email_id} sends a specific email to a specific subscriber
tooling: curl or any HTTP client; there is no official SDK, and typed clients are generated from the OpenAPI spec
chaining: a list sender rather than a transactional relay: every recipient is a subscriber, so it carries a newsletter or a notification list of up to 100 people, and per-message transactional mail belongs on a relay.

limits.value: the free price assumes at most one email a day to the whole subscriber base; more needs a contact with the vendor
600 API requests per minute on every endpoint, and 100 subscriber creations per day through POST /v1/subscribers
every new account is reviewed before it can send, most reviews within one to three business days
new senders are capped per hour until they reach a baseline of engagement and reputation; the figure is not stated

limits_note: counts of things, not rates, so no vocabulary kind names them: 100 subscribers on the free plan.

identity_cost.detail: The register page asks for a username, an email address and a password, or Apple or Google sign-in, and states that no card is needed. Every new account is reviewed before it can send, and a verification form asks what the newsletter is about, who its audience is, where imported subscribers came from, and details of the person or organization. No domain is needed: mail goes out from the username at buttondown.email by default. A custom sending domain is free, set up either by delegating a subdomain with two NS records (managed) or by adding the records shown in settings (manual).

reliability_note: sending is disabled temporarily when unsubscribes, complaints or hard bounces run high on a new sender
